text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Tehran demands apology from Bonn in row over dissident assassination trial; religious students in Iran demand death sentence against German prosecutors
- Doctors protest against cuts in pharmaceuticals budget
- Germany and Bosnia sign agreement on repatriation of refugees
- Court rules transfer fees for sportsmen and sportswomen are illegal
- Christian Democrat deputies want to halve coal subsidy by 2000
- M3 money supply continues to grow too strongly
- Christian Democrats want to limit number of low-paid "590 mark" jobs
- Finance Minister Waigel says federal states will not raise public spending in 1997
HANDELSBLATT
- Ifo institute says economic sentiment improving in western Germany
- Christian Democrat deputies want to scrap coal subsidy
- German federal prosecutors threatened in Iran
- Deutsche Telekom share flotation pushes up money supply
- President Herzog offers China help with reform of legal system
- Brussels wants uniform telephone numbering system for EU
- Metallgesellschaft to sell company bank
- Bankruptcies to hit new record this year
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Iranian mullahs issue death threats against German prosecutors
- Bonn knew about activities of sometime agent Werner Mauss to free German hostage in Colombia
- Germany and Bosnia sign agreement on repatriation of refugees
- Confectionery industry faces strike over sick pay
- More and more Germans threatened by debt burden
- Deutsche Telekom share flotation pushes up money supply
DIE WELT
- Doctors protest against cuts in pharmaceuticals budget
- North Rhine-Westphalia state premier Rau threatens to dissolve Social Democrat coalition with Greens
- Foreign Minister Kinkel says it would be mistake to break off relations with Iran
- Christian Democrat parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble calls on employers to create more jobs
- Industry federation chairman Henkel calls for tough pay round in 1997 and end of attempts to find consensus with workers
- Economic recovery lacks impetus
- German firms double foreign investment
- Unions criticise Social Democrats over suggestion of lower starting wage for long-term unemployed
